newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European share strength pegged back by Dow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European share strength pegged back by Dow.

text.p: Europe's key stock markets rose strongly on Wednesday, but stepped back from their session highs after Wall Street failed to build upon record overnight gains.

European bourses raced ahead at the open and held the bulk of this rally over the day, with London ignoring a call for higher interest rates to end at a five-week high and Madrid hitting an all-time record.
The Ibex-35 of Spanish blue-chips ended 72.23 higher at 5,802.26 points.

A sprinkling of good corporate results also lifted sentiment and both Frankfurt and Paris ending well-ahead, shrugging off a comprehensively leaked European Commission report that all but Italy and Greece would meet the targets to join a European single currency.
This also got scant attention from the currency market, where the dollar ended slightly lower against the mark and yen after a sluggish session.
The Lira suffered briefly from the EC forecast, but nerves were soothed by a footnote indicating that Italy could still meet a 1997 budget deficit-to-GDP target of 3.0 percent.
The stock market tone was set by Wall Street's huge overnight rally, which pushed the Dow Jones industrial 173.38 points higher to 6,833.59 -- its second largest day-gain.
A spate of better than expected corporate results did the rest.
Dutch electronics giant Philips aided a two percent gain in shares in Amsterdam after a sharp profits gain pushed its shares above 100 guilders and to an all-time high.
Profit-taking limited the rally but the AEX index still closed over 1.30 percent higher at 759.

Shrugging off the Bank of England's call for a quarter percentage point rise in interest rates to counter the threat of inflation, the FTSE 100 index closed up 39.7 points at 4,385.8, with gainers in a four-to-one majority.
Barclays helped the advance after Tuesday's upbeat trading statement, leading other bank stocks higher. Insurers also rose, spurred by an upgrade on Royal Sun from Goldman Sachs.
French shares also closed firm, although profit-taking on the last trading day for settlement in April meant the CAC index failed to break through resistance at 2,550.
It ended up 18.97 points or 0.75 percent at 2,533.64. The CAC-40 futures contract was up 21 at 2,536 from Tuesday's close.
French President Jacques Chirac on Monday declared snap parliamentary elections to be held in a matter of weeks.

But the political fallout from this high-stakes gamble was seen waning for the time being after an opinion poll showed the centre-right coalition being returned with a solid, albeit reduced, majority.
CURRENCIES AT 1730 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7115 marks and 126.10 yen after ending at 1.7131 and 126.21 in late trading in Europe on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1730 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 41.6 points or 0.96 percent at 4,387.7
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended bourse floor trade up 55.62 points or 1.67 percent at 3,395.95.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 18.97 points or 0.75 percent at 2,533.64.
PRECIOUS METALS
GOLD - Fixed slightly higher at $341.00 from $340.70. Market edges up after initial fall on increasingly bearish sentiment. SILVER - Static. Three cents lower with gold at $4.72/$4.74.
